scenes.text: The Moon is leaving us. Right now.
Every year, it drifts about four centimeters farther away.
That's roughly how fast your fingernails grow.
We know because Apollo astronauts left mirrors up there.
Scientists bounce lasers off them and time the trip.
The culprit? Tides. Earth's oceans tug on the Moon and slowly fling it outward.
And the Moon pulls back, slowing our spin. Our days keep getting longer.
Billions of years ago, the Moon looked far bigger in the sky.
Someday, it will look too small to fully cover the Sun.
Total solar eclipses will end. Hundreds of millions of years from now.
So go look at one while you can. Comment if you'd miss it.
